records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` combined with `max_processes or len(...)` means a `--flusher-processes 0` value silently degrades to one process per shard (the maximum), inverting the operator's intent. An operator setting `--flusher-processes 0` expecting to disable the multi-process flusher instead spawns the largest possible number of Redis-connected flusher processes, one per shard, multiplying COGS and Redis connections on a path that was previously single-process.
records.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit `max_processes=0` as falsy and replaces it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, spawning one process per shard. Since the new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is `type=int` with no validation preventing `0`, this is a real, diff-verifiable behavior inversion for the operator-provided value `0`.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] submit() now emits metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure") once per backpressured process per submit call instead of once, inflating the counter by the number of processes whenever more than one flusher is backpressured. Operators relying on the backpressure metric's rate to gauge severity see N-times-inflated counts under the multi-process default, distorting alerting thresholds the moment flusher_processes > 1 ships.
records.rationale: The diff shows `submit()` loops over `self.process_backpressure_since.values()`, but it increments the metric and immediately exits on the *first* backpressured process: `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure")` followed by `raise MessageRejected()`. Because of this immediate `raise`, it cannot emit the metric “once per backpressured process per submit call” as claimed; at most one increment occurs per `submit()` invocation.

records.issue_text: [BUG] On the threading path (produce_to_pipe mode), a hung flusher thread is never terminated before a replacement is started, so two threads poll the same shards and produce duplicate spans. `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False for Thread, so the kill is skipped; `_create_process_for_shards` starts a new thread for the same shard list while the hung 'unhealthy' one is still alive, and both poll Redis and produce the same segments to Kafka — downstream consumers get duplicated span payloads, and repeated hang-restarts accumulate hung threads.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep to a lambda returning None, so the flusher thread gets zero guaranteed time to process after the drift change. test_basic intermittently fails in CI: the flusher thread races the main thread's step.join() with no actual wait, producing flaky failures exactly like the flakiness this sleep was presumably meant to fix.
records.rationale: In `test_basic`, the test patches `time.sleep` to a no-op (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`). The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` therefore does not actually wait, so it cannot provide any guaranteed time for the flusher thread to run after `fac._flusher.current_drift.value = 9000`. The main thread can proceed immediately to `step.join()`, which sets the flusher `stopped` flag and can race the background thread’s processing, making the intended flakiness fix ineffective.

records.issue_text: [BUG] join() waits sequentially on each process against a shared absolute deadline and breaks out of the loop without terminating or waiting for the remaining processes once the deadline passes. With N flusher processes and a join timeout T, the first slow process consumes the entire T; all subsequent processes are skipped via `break` and never receive terminate(), so spawned processes/thread flushers stay alive past shutdown and any in-flight segments in their shards are dropped — a consumer restart loses data. No test in the diff exercises join() with more than the fast path, so this is unverified.
records.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the new loop over `self.processes` uses a shared absolute `deadline` and explicitly `break`s once `remaining_time <= 0` (see: `if remaining_time <= 0: break`). That means any processes/threads after the first slow one are skipped entirely: they are neither waited on (`while process.is_alive()...`) nor terminated (`if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()`). This is a behavior regression relative to the single-process case and can leave flusher workers alive past shutdown.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` only kills `multiprocessing.Process` instances; when `produce_to_pipe` is set the flusher runs as a `threading.Thread`, and a hung thread is left running while `_create_process_for_shards` immediately starts a replacement on the same shards. Two threads poll Redis for the same shards concurrently, so segments can be flushed/produced twice or torn between the old and new thread; the 'unhealthy' condition that triggered the restart is never actually cleared in thread mode, so every subsequent submit() spawns yet another duplicate thread until MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS raises RuntimeError.
